title: The open public Wi-Fi network — question explanation
learningObjective: Choose safer connection practices and avoid exposing sensitive data on untrusted networks
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: At an airport, several similarly named free Wi-Fi networks appear. You need to access a sensitive work account.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Choose safer connection practices and avoid exposing sensitive data on untrusted networks
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option C: Use a personal or organization-approved hotspot, or a verified network with required protections. Prefer a trusted connection; public wireless networks can expose devices and traffic to additional risk.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: HTTPS protects data in transit to a valid site but does not authenticate the Wi-Fi operator or protect against every threat. Option B: Signal strength does not verify who operates the network. Option D: Disabling a security control does not improve trust in the network and increases exposure.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Prefer mobile data or an organization-approved hotspot. Follow your organization’s VPN and remote-access requirements. Network names and signal strength do not prove that a Wi-Fi network is legitimate.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Network names and signal strength do not prove that a Wi-Fi network is legitimate.
